analysis: Documentation-only PR: docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md (date bump at line 3, new delta-checkpoint paragraph at lines 526-528) and docs/architecture/security/encryption.md (date bump, new claim near line 121-122). No source or control code changed, so no code-level regression is visible. The new text says that on native recurrent layouts a request which consumed a restore stores later checkpoints as deltas of the restored file, and a restore reads the chain forward. It also says a delta names its parent only through a keyed commitment, so files of one conversation stay unlinkable without the cache key. This touches T-041 (cache at-rest metadata, leak #2 class, HMAC-keyed names, KEK purge) and A-001. The T-041 detail says nothing prompt-derived beyond the keyed lookupTag may be added to DBK3 metadata/AAD. The delta-parent commitment is described as keyed, which is consistent with that rule, but the implementation (SSDHybridCheckpointStore Write/Read, DBK3 format) is not in the supplied evidence. Open questions for deeper review: (1) whether the parent commitment is truly derived under K_lookup or similar with scope folded in; (2) chain-restore authentication: each link must be AES-GCM authenticated and bound to tenant/cacheSalt/model identity so a replayed or swapped parent cannot be spliced; (3) TTL/LRU eviction of a parent while a child survives must fall back cold rather than serve partial state; (4) T-041 may need a note that delta chains add file-count and size-linkage metadata. These are unverified contracts, not findings, because no code was supplied. No new endpoint or trust boundary changes were seen. needs_deeper_review is set because the cryptographic claim cannot be verified from docs alone.
